minor.issue: When the 20s circuit-breaker cache (_FAIL_CACHE_SEC) expires, the very next request re-probes MySQL and blocks up to ~20s (wait_for(15s) + connect_timeout overhead) before returning 503. Subsequent requests within the new 20s window are instant again. So a user attempting login exactly at the reset boundary can experience one slow response every ~20-35s. Recommendation: reduce asyncio.wait_for timeout in services/__init__.py from 15s to 3-5s (and connect_timeout from 10s to 3s) so the periodic reset-probe becomes near-instant. Not a regression from prior fixes — the app is bounded and never hangs indefinitely — but worth tightening for perceived UX. Reference: /app/backend/services/__init__.py:35,46 and :63,74

action_items: OPTIONAL (UX polish): In /app/backend/services/__init__.py reduce `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=15)` to timeout=3 and aiomysql `connect_timeout=10` to 3 for both init_patron_pool and init_data_pool. This shrinks the worst-case probe from ~20s to ~3s at the circuit-breaker reset boundary. Circuit breaker cache (20s) can stay as-is.

critical_code_review_comments: services/__init__.py: init_patron_pool and init_data_pool both call aiomysql.create_pool with connect_timeout=10 wrapped in asyncio.wait_for(timeout=15). Since the MySQL handshake stalls (not TCP), aiomysql waits the full connect_timeout=10 for the auth handshake then wait_for(15) provides the outer bound. Consider dropping both to 3s for faster fail-fast.
services/__init__.py: The `_FAIL_CACHE_SEC = 20` circuit breaker constant is well-chosen but could be exposed via env var for tuning without code change.
server.py:231: `app.state.init_pools_task = asyncio.create_task(_init_pools_bg())` — the critical GC-safety fix is correctly applied and documented in comments.

server.py:45-54: Global RuntimeError → 503 handler is a good defensive net but relies on substring match 'ulaşılamıyor'. Consider raising a dedicated exception class (e.g. `DBUnreachableError(RuntimeError)`) and matching on isinstance instead of message content to prevent silent regressions if the message wording changes.

rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by E1 and re-verified this iteration): User's remote MySQL server at 185.223.77.132:3306 is in a half-broken state — the TCP listener accepts connections (SYN-ACK completes in ~0.12s) but mysqld never writes the initial handshake greeting packet. Raw socket recv() times out. This is a server-side issue on the USER'S VPS (likely mysqld hung, out-of-memory, hitting max_connections, or an iptables/hosts.allow change). Fixable only by the user on their VPS (restart mysqld, check /var/log/mysql/error.log, verify slow queries, check disk/RAM). SECONDARY BUGS E1 FIXED (verified working this iteration): (1) `asyncio.create_task(_init_pools_bg())` now saved to `app.state.init_pools_task` so the task is not garbage-collected mid-flight (previously caused 'Task was destroyed but it is pending!' and every request hanging forever); (2) `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=15)` around `aiomysql.create_pool` prevents the pool init coroutine from blocking indefinitely; (3) `_FAIL_CACHE_SEC=20` circuit breaker in services/__init__.py short-circuits repeated attempts to ~0ms; (4) global RuntimeError → HTTP 503 handler in server.py returns clear Turkish JSON `{kod: DB_UNREACHABLE}` instead of a generic 500.
